chunks: Therefore, hasten with your ears towards it,
and intensify your efforts for it. Make it a substitute for all your past (shortcomings) to take their place as a successor, and make it your supporter against every opponent.

Turn your sleep into wakefulness by its help, and pass your days with it. Make it the equipment of your hearts, wash your sins with it, treat your ailments with it and hasten towards your death with it.
Take a lesson from him who neglects it, so that others who follow it should not take a lesson from you (i.e., from your neglecting it).
Beware, therefore; you should take care of it and should take care of yourselves through it.

key_terms.الْحِمَامَ: The deathbed / The grave (literally: the bathhouse)

ai.seo_question: How does one use wisdom or the Quran to atone for past shortcomings and cure spiritual ailments?
ai.summary: In this passage from the Sermon of the Quran, Imam Ali (AS) personifies the Quran as a living entity, urging believers to actively internalize it through intense listening and diligent application, thereby transforming it into a spiritual remedy for sins and a guide for conduct. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the Quran not merely as a text to be recited, but as a dynamic source of wisdom (Hikmah) that demands total engagement of the senses and heart to cure spiritual ailments and prepare the soul for the Hereafter.
